from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Space is the same; coordinate descriptions differ.",
            "Imagine a point viewed through different rulers.",
            "Standard grid lines define our default perspective.",
            "Switching basis changes the coordinate numbers.",
            "The vector stays put; labels just shift."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Concept of 'Perspective'", lecture_lines)
        
        # Initialize objects
        square = Square(side_length=1.5, color=WHITE)
        point = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        vanishing_point = Dot(color=RED).move_to(self.grid["C5"])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.place_in_area(square, "B4", "E6")
        self.play(Create(square))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(ORANGE)
        self.play(FadeIn(vanishing_point))
        lines = VGroup(*[Line(square.get_corner(corner), vanishing_point.get_center(), color="#7F7F7F", stroke_width=2) 
                        for corner in [UL, UR, DL, DR]])
        self.play(Create(lines))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(square.animate.shift(0.5 * LEFT + 0.5 * UP))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(PURPLE)
        self.place_at_grid(point, "C5", 1.0)
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(point))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):

            "The change of basis matrix bridges systems.",
            "Matrix multiplication maps coordinates across perspectives."

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Deriving the Calculation Process", [
            "Equation: the vector in A equals P times B.",
            "Matrix P columns are basis vectors in A.",
            "Basis vectors serve as the transformation's building blocks."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Equation: the vector in A equals P times B.
        eq = MathTex(r"[v]_A = P \cdot [v]_B", font_size=40)
        self.place_in_area(eq, 'A1', 'B6')
        self.play(Write(eq))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#3498DB")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Matrix P columns are basis vectors in A.
        p_matrix = MathTex(r"P = \begin{bmatrix} | & | \\ b_1 & b_2 \\ | & | \end{bmatrix}", font_size=36)
        self.place_in_area(p_matrix, 'C1', 'D6')
        self.play(Write(p_matrix))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#F1C40F")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Basis vectors serve as the transformation's building blocks.
        highlight = SurroundingRectangle(p_matrix, color="#2ECC71", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(highlight))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#2ECC71")
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Practical Application & Summary", [
            "Choosing a smart basis simplifies complex motion.",
            "Rotation is just scaling in the right basis.",
            "Change of basis reveals the simplest perspective."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        robot_arm = Rectangle(width=2, height=0.5, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.5)
        math_box = MathTex(r"T = \begin{bmatrix} \cos \theta & -\sin \theta \\ \sin \theta & \cos \theta \end{bmatrix}", font_size=36)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#F1C40F")
        self.place_in_area(robot_arm, 'B2', 'C5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(robot_arm))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#3498DB")
        self.play(FadeOut(robot_arm))
        self.place_in_area(math_box, 'B2', 'C5', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(math_box))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#2ECC71")
        math_box_highlight = SurroundingRectangle(math_box, color="#2ECC71", buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(math_box_highlight))
        self.play(math_box_highlight.animate.set_stroke(width=6))
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: The Concept of 'Perspective' (Prerequisite Review)
sections.content: Define a basis as a coordinate system (a set of rulers). Explain that the same point in space can be described by different numbers depending on which 'rulers' we use. Visual: An animation of a 2D plane showing a point P with coordinates (2, 3) relative to standard grid lines, then shifting the grid lines.
sections.example: Imagine a cat sitting on a rug. If you measure its position relative to the room's corner (Basis A), it's (2, 2). If you measure it relative to the rug's corner (Basis B), it's (1, 1).

sections.title: The Transition Matrix (The Bridge)
sections.content: Introduce the Change of Basis matrix (P). Explain that P acts as a 'translator' that converts coordinates from the new basis to the old basis (or vice versa). Visual: An animated flow chart where a vector v in Basis B is 'multiplied' by matrix P to emerge as the same vector in Basis A.
sections.example: A GPS device uses WGS84 coordinates. To show the location on a local city map (a different basis), the device multiplies the global coordinates by a specific transition matrix.

sections.title: Deriving the Calculation Process
sections.content: Show the formal equation: [v]_A = P * [v]_B. Explain that P is composed of columns representing the basis vectors of B written in terms of Basis A. Visual: A split-screen showing vectors b1 and b2 being broken down into components of standard basis e1 and e2.
sections.example: If Basis B = { (1,1), (0,1) }, the matrix P = [[1, 0], [1, 1]]. Mapping a point (2, 3) from B to A becomes a simple matrix multiplication.

sections.title: Practical Application & Summary
sections.content: Briefly mention that choosing the 'right' basis can simplify complex problems (like diagonalization). Recap: Change of basis doesn't change the vector, just our description of it. Visual: A complex rotation problem where the math looks messy in the standard basis but becomes a simple scaling operation in a rotated basis.
sections.example: A robot arm (character) rotates its 'hand' to grab an object. By changing the basis to the hand's orientation, the calculation for the grasp becomes trivial compared to calculating it from the floor's perspective.
